article.title: Former Bolivian VP granted political asylum by Mexico
article.author: Pablo Meriguet
article.content: Former Bolivian vice president Álvaro García Linera is currently in Mexico where he has been granted political asylum. Shortly after, the Bolivian Attorney General’s Office requested Interpol issue a Blue Notice to locate García Linera for alleged crimes of murder and torture. This was reported by Police Commander Adrián Álvarez. For his part, presidential spokesperson José Luis Gálvez said that García Linera had left the country, first to Argentina and then to Mexico. García Linera himself reported on Friday that Mexico has granted his request for political asylum: “I am in Mexico and I have political asylum in Mexico.” This is not the first time Mexico has granted this status to the former vice president. Back in 2019, following the coup against Morales, both top leaders of the MAS arrived in Mexico from Bolivia under asylum status. According to the state prosecutors , Evo Morales (the country’s former president from 2006 to 2019) and García Linera were responsible for the police raid on a hotel in Santa Cruz in 2009, in which three people were killed. Meanwhile, the government at the time said that the police succeeded in dismantling a terrorist and separatist cell. The three people killed were accused of being part of a cell that sought to carry out terrorist operations to promote the secession of the Santa Cruz region from Bolivia. An arrest warrant has been outstanding against Evo Morales for several months for other alleged crimes, but the former president has decided to remain in Bolivia, surrounded by his supporters, and has not yet been apprehended by the police. Morales has denounced the charges against him as a clear act of political persecution against the leaders of the progressive MAS (Movement Toward Socialism) government, which succeeded in establishing the first government led by an Indigenous person in the history of Bolivia – one of the countries with the highest concentration of Indigenous people in the world. Regarding the charges in the case involving García Linera, Morales said : “I’m not going to leave [the country]; I’m going to face the music; I’m going to defend myself; we’re going to defend the unity of the national territory against those who want to divide it – that’s why they’re prosecuting me.” Unlike Morales, who has maintained a clearly influential public profile in Bolivia’s political landscape, García Linera has devoted himself primarily to academic activities, though he has always expressed his political views on current events. García Linera is widely recognized as one of the most important critical and intellectual voices not only in Bolivia but throughout Latin America. The Supreme Court of Justice has warned that if García Linera does not appear in court, he will be declared “in contempt,” which would justify his arrest. And based on the sequence of events, it appears that this will indeed be the prosecution’s decision. For its part, the Bolivian Ministry of Foreign Affairs has requested an explanation from Mexico regarding the as-yet-unconfirmed political asylum granted to García Linera, and warned that the possible decision will not halt the judicial investigations into a case that many claim is more about political persecution than anything else, although the Bolivian government asserts that it is a process aimed at seeking justice. Nadia Beller , Bolivian attorney and ex-girlfriend of right-wing political operative Fernando Cerimedo also requested and was granted political asylum in Mexico.
